title: DS spec clause
description: One numbered spec paragraph. Per STYL.5.3. `text` is the verbatim Markdown span (lossless render); all other fields are derived/authored metadata.

id.description: Canonical clause ID; equals the filename stem (STYL.2.1). A segment is digits with an optional lowercase tail.

prefix.description: 4-5 letter prefix; tree derives from prefix[0] (STYL.5.2.2).

parent.description: Enclosing clause ID; null for a top-level (PFX.N) item.

seq.description: Physical (document) order. Render sort key, decoupled from numeric ID (STYL.2.8.5).

kind.description: Spec-beat class (STYL.5.3.2); decides whether a check is expected. `tombstone` is a retired ID's stub (empty text).

heading.description: Section title when kind=heading or the item leads with a titled header; else null.

text.description: The clause's Markdown body (verbatim span incl. its ID tag).

deferred.description: Written only as `true`: the obligation does not bind this edition (STYL.5.3.3). Absent means it binds. Whether a clause is ratified is derived, never stored.

compiler_only.description: Written only as `true`: everything the clause states is the compiler's verdict on a program (STYL.5.3.11.1), so a `compile_ok` vector can ratify it (STYL.5.3.11). Only a normative, definition, observation or table clause carries it.

also_ids.description: Additional clause IDs co-defined in this clause's header (a multi-ID header, STYL.2.6); they share this clause's text span and get no separate file.

refs.description: Clause IDs cited by this item's prose (extracted from [ID] tokens).

defines.description: Identifiers this clause is the single authoritative definer of, per registry (STYL.5.3.5.1). Consumed by the registry-sync gate (STYL.5.9).

checks.description: Verification ties to models and notations: tool -> array of check objects (STYL.5.3.6). Conformance tests are not stored here: their links are on the test side and derived on every load.

asdl.description: An ASDL definition of a syntax tree a tool exchanges, by path + type or constructor name (STYL.2.15.2).

jsonschema.description: A JSON Schema of a document a tool writes, by path + `$defs` name, or `null` for the whole document (STYL.2.15.2).

data.description: Structured source for a clause whose `text` block is GENERATED from it (STYL.5.3.2.1). Two shapes, discriminated by which key is present — a registry TABLE, or an EBNF grammar. `additionalProperties: false` on both arms is what makes presence a discriminator rather than a hint: a mixed object validates against neither.

oneOf.description: A registry table. The Markdown pipe table in `text` is rendered from it.

An EBNF grammar. The fenced ```ebnf block in `text` is rendered from it. THE SOURCE, not a path: a path would make the clause a pointer to the authority instead of the authority (EBNFFOLD1, implementer's answer).

verification.description: Coverage verdict; derived unless asserted (STYL.5.3.7). `refuted` is ASSERTED ONLY and is never derived: a clause shown false by a proof is not a coverage state, and no count of passing checks can produce it.

name.description: Element inside the file (sig / operator / K program label / test id / proto message); null for a file-level tie.

model_check.description: An Alloy or TLA+ tie. Structure (`path`, `name`, `tag`) is derived from the model tags and regenerated by `spec_crossref.py --write`; `verdict`, `counterexample` and `note` are AUTHORED and merged across a write, exactly as on the idris lane. A bounded model can prove a clause within its scope, prove less than the clause claims, show the clause false, or show that the IMPLEMENTATION breaks a clause that stands, and `verdict` says which.

name.description: The element inside the file: an Alloy sig / fact / check / run, a TLA+ operator / VARIABLE / CONSTANT.

verdict.description: What the check concluded, when the author has said. OPTIONAL: the default reading of a green bounded check is STYL.5.5.4's tie -- the property holds within the model's scope -- and most entries say nothing more. `proven` -- the property holds within the model's scope and establishes the clause. `refuted` -- the CLAUSE is false; `counterexample` is then required and the clause must carry `verification: "refuted"`. `partial` -- the model and the clause do not coincide, in either direction; `note` says how. `violated` -- the clause STANDS and the model shows the IMPLEMENTATION breaking it; `counterexample` is then required, and the clause's `verification` is untouched because the finding is about the code, not the corpus. `assumed` is deliberately absent: it names a hole in a proof term, which a bounded model has none of; a model whose property rests on an asserted fact is `partial`, with the assumption in its note.

counterexample.description: Required when verdict is refuted or violated: the witness -- a TLC trace or an Alloy instance, in prose -- stated so a reader can check it without running the tool.

idris_check.description: An Idris tie. Every other lane records WHETHER a clause is checked; this one also records WHAT THE CHECK CONCLUDED, because a proof assistant can conclude the clause is false and no other surface in this corpus can express that -- and WHAT KIND OF ELEMENT concluded it, because the STYL.5.5.4 name rule makes every column-0 element an entry, so without a `role` a hundred list lemmas read as a hundred proofs of the clause.

name.description: The named element inside the module. NOT nullable, unlike `check.name`: Idris is an ELEMENT surface, so a file-level tie is not expressible and the STYL.5.5.4 name rule has nothing to check without it.

role.description: What kind of element this is. REQUIRED, with no default. `definition` -- a data / record / interface declaration or a function that models the clause's vocabulary; it establishes nothing by itself. `lemma` -- a helper step (a list or arithmetic fact, an unfolding) used by a theorem; it establishes nothing about the clause on its own. `theorem` -- the element that states and discharges a claim of the clause, quantified over its inputs. `witness` -- a concrete instance or refutation: a `Refl` on literals, an `impossible` case, an executed history; it establishes exactly one point. Coverage counts theorems and witnesses; a definition or a lemma is bookkeeping toward them.

verdict.description: What the element concluded. REQUIRED for a `theorem` or a `witness`, with no default and no derivation; OPTIONAL for a `definition` or a `lemma` that is sound. `proven` -- it typechecks and establishes the clause. `refuted` -- the clause is FALSE; `counterexample` is then required. `violated` -- the clause stands and the element shows the IMPLEMENTATION breaking it; `counterexample` is then required and the clause's `verification` is untouched. `assumed` -- the element rests on a postulate, believe_me, assert_total or assert_smaller, so it is a statement of intent rather than a proof; recorded on EVERY role, because an unlabelled hole carries a type checker's authority whatever kind of element hides it. `partial` -- the element and the clause do not coincide, in either direction, per the [LFST.4.6] precedent.

counterexample.description: Required when verdict is refuted or violated: the witness, stated so a reader can check it without running Idris.
